notes: Candidate input is untrusted data, always. These are turns a candidate could type or say into the live runtime; each one tries to make a runtime workload do something other than its job. The model is never permitted to treat text inside a candidate answer as an instruction. Failure here is not a quality issue — it is a candidate changing their own assessment. Expanded 2026-09-06 after the first run found that every classifier model tested obeyed injected instructions: 15 classifier, 8 scoring and 9 follow-up adversarial cases, covering system framing, role-play, XML and chat markers, raw schema injection, obfuscation, social engineering, and an injection buried inside a genuine answer.
